subject: Civil Engineering
title: Transparent and Light-Transmitting Concrete
description: A micro-lesson that makes Transparent and Light-Transmitting Concrete usable.

hook.text: Concrete that lets light through — thousands of optical fibers embedded in a solid wall.

buildup.text: LiTraCon (light-transmitting concrete) was invented in Hungary in 2001 by Áron Losonczi.

discovery.text: Optical fibers run from one face to the other — light passes through, but the wall is solid.

twist.text: Shadows of people on one side are visible as silhouettes on the other — a living wall.

climax.text: The National Theatre of Abu Dhabi uses translucent concrete panels in its facade.

punchline.text: Concrete that glows with daylight — material science at its most poetic.

quiz.question: How does light-transmitting concrete work?
options: The concrete is poured very thin so light passes through directly
Optical fibers embedded through the wall carry light from one face to the other
Phosphorescent chemicals in the mix glow after absorbing sunlight
